editorial:
Imagine working your fingers to the bone just to give your kid a better life, only for that kid to turn into a total nightmare. That is exactly what you get with this classic. You follow Mildred, a brave mom who leaves her lazy husband to start her own cake business. She builds a huge success from nothing, but her daughter, Veda, is spoiled and cruel. The movie feels like a slow-burn drama that suddenly turns into a tense crime story. You will feel for Mildred because she tries so hard to be a good parent, but Veda just wants money and status, making their relationship feel like a battle.

The acting is top-notch, especially the way the daughter manipulates everyone around her. While some parts feel a bit slow, the mystery of the murder keeps you leaning in. If you enjoy old-school movies with high stakes and family drama, you will love this one. Since it is an older film, you should try to find it in a restored version. It makes those sharp black-and-white shots look amazing on a big screen.
endingExplained: At the end, you find out that Veda actually killed her wealthy husband for his money. She tried to pin the crime on Mildred to get her out of the way. However, the police eventually find the truth through some clever detective work. Veda is arrested and sent away, while Mildred finally finds some peace. It is a sad ending because Mildred realized her love for her daughter was used against her.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves strong lead characters and twisty mysteries.
